2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - How AppMenus (fork-owned) rearranges OrcaSlicer's wxMenus:
     - `arrange()` and `without()` place and remove items.
     - `stock_item()` finds an item by label.
     - A new `stock_keyed_item()` matches labels that end with kShownKey plus a rebindable key.
   - wx update-UI ordering: a handler bound later runs first. AppMenus binds wxEVT_UPDATE_UI on the frame for an OrcaSlicer item and doesn't Skip, so it overrides OrcaSlicer's always-true condition.
   - The Mac hides Quit in the File menu, so no separator before it.
   - The Edit menu title uses `_L_CONTEXT("Edit", "Menu")`.
   - Plater::export_gcode(false) writes .gcode. EVT_GLTOOLBAR_EXPORT_SLICED_FILE writes .gcode.3mf.
   - Generic 3MF uses export_3mf with Silence. Project 3MF uses SplitModel|ShareMesh|Silence.
   - Reading the live Mac menus through the AX JXA script `dump_menus.js` (reads properties in bulk), clicking with `click_menu.js`, and the MCP workspace_inspect plate count through `inspect.py` (uses tests/mcp/probe.py `call`).

     - UI actions run as a scheduled task with Interactive logon as guitest.

       ```cpp
       wxMenuItem* stock_keyed_item(wxMenu* menu, const wxString& label)
       {
           const wxString text = wxStripMenuCodes(label);
           for (wxMenuItem* item : menu->GetMenuItems())
               if (!item->IsSeparator() && (item->GetItemLabelText() == text || item->GetItemLabelText().StartsWith(text + kShownKey)))
                   return item;
           throw std::runtime_error(...);
       }
       ```

       ```cpp
       {
       #ifdef __APPLE__
           wxMenu* edit = bar_menu(m_frame, _L_CONTEXT("Edit", "Menu"));
       #else
           wxMenu* edit = top_submenu(m_frame, _L_CONTEXT("Edit", "Menu"));
       #endif
           const int id = stock_item(edit, _L("Duplicate Current Plate"))->GetId();
           m_frame.Bind(wxEVT_UPDATE_UI, &AppMenus::on_update_ui, this, id);
           m_bound.emplace_back(edit, id);
           m_commands.emplace(id, Command{{}, [this] { return !home(); }});
       ```

content.text:
I got Import wrong in both rounds of menu work. When I rebuilt the menus, my code moved the Import item into place in the File menu but never looked inside it. Then, when you asked me to trim items, I went through Export item by item and skipped Import. So the submenu you saw is still OrcaSlicer's, plus two printer-import items that earlier JusPrin commits had added to it (b0a2fe3b08 on 6 November and c2de39168b on 8 November).

A separate code reader went through the submenu, and I checked its main findings against the code myself. Nothing below has been run in the app.

**What's wrong:**

1. **The empty grey squares and the uneven indent.**
   - OrcaSlicer gives ZIP and Configs an icon called `menu_import`, which is a blank, almost fully transparent 16×16 square. The two JusPrin items copied that icon.
   - On the Mac, OrcaSlicer gives the first item no icon. The Mac indents items that have a picture, so the first item sits flush left and the other four are pushed right.
   - Both points are confirmed in the code (`MainFrame.cpp`, lines 3127–3142).
2. **"Import from OrcaSlicer…" and "Import from JusPrin 1…" don't import files.** They open the printer-import window. Only the hidden item description says "printers"; the Mac doesn't show that text.
3. **"Import Configs…" overlaps with both of those.** It loads OrcaSlicer profile files (printer and filament settings), under a word OrcaSlicer users know and other people don't. In the trim I removed the matching Preset Bundle export but left this import.
4. **"Import ZIP Archive…" is never greyed out.** OrcaSlicer's call leaves out the argument that links the item to its enable check, so the check never runs. That bug comes from upstream.
5. **On Home, the first item and ⌘I are enabled.** Reading the code, choosing a model there would add it to whichever project sits hidden behind Home and switch to that project. I greyed out Duplicate Current Plate on Home for exactly this reason and missed Import. I haven't reproduced this in the app yet.
6. **The first item's label is misleading.** It lists six formats while the dialog accepts twelve or more. It also overlaps with File › Open…, and neither label says which one starts a new project.
7. **The tests miss all of this.** They only check that the two "Import from…" items exist.

**Decision needed:** how File › Import should look. This is your call because it changes wording and moves items between menus. The fixes would be small, though two of them would touch OrcaSlicer's `MainFrame.cpp`. My proposal:
- **Model imports:** grey out the first item and the ZIP item on Home, after I reproduce the problem there.
- **Icons:** remove the blank icon from all five items, so the Mac lines them up.
- **Printer imports:** move the two "Import from…" items to the Printer menu next to Add a printer…, labelled "Import printers from OrcaSlicer…" and "Import printers from JusPrin 1…". Two error messages spell out the old File › Import menu path, so I would update those too.
- **Import Configs…:** hide it in JusPrin's view, as I did with the export.

That would leave File › Import with two items: models, and ZIP. The other option is to only fix the icons and the Home greying and keep the current labels. That costs less, but the confusing wording stays.

My pick is the full proposal.
Yes, as proposed

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".

"""One harness run. Returns whether the page's part of it passed, what
    failed in that part, how many checks passed, and what failed elsewhere.

    An entry with "checks" depends on those named checks alone: the run is
    stopped once they have passed, and a failure elsewhere in it is reported
    apart, since it is not about the page. Without "checks" the whole run
    has to pass. The harness gives up by itself after 900 s."""
    args = [str(out) if arg == "{dir}" else arg for arg in entry["args"]]
    env = dict(os.environ, **{name: str(out) if value == "{dir}" else value for name, value in entry.get("env", {}).items()})
    needed = set(entry.get("checks", []))
    if needed:
        # A run stopped early never removes its data folder, which the harness makes in the
        # temporary folder: put that beside the run, to remove it here. Only for these runs:
        # the printer menu's run takes ten minutes instead of six seconds with it moved.
        env["TMPDIR"] = str(out / "data")
        (out / "data").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    passed, failed, lines = set(), [], []
    process = subprocess.Popen([str(binary), *args], env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                               text=True, errors="replace")
    for line in process.stdout:
        lines.append(line)
        check = re.search(r"HARNESS CHECK (\S+) (PASS|FAIL)", line)
        if check:
            (passed.add if check.group(2) == "PASS" else failed.append)(check.group(1))
        if needed and (needed <= passed or needed & set(failed)):
            process.terminate()
